In mathematics, '''quantum algebra''' is the study of noncommutative analogues and generalizations of [[Commutative algebra (structure)|commutative algebras]], especially those arising in [[Lie theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathoverflow.net/a/290525/36146|title=What is quantum algebra?|website=mathoverflow.net|access-date=2018-01-22}}</ref>. It is one of the top-level mathematics categories used by the [[arXiv]], and is a unification of algebraic deformations, [[Hopf algebra]]s, [[category theory]], [[topology]], [[noncommutative geometry]], and [[quantum group]]s within [[quantum mechanics]] and [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum Algebra |url=https://arxiv.org/list/math.QA/recent |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=arxiv.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum Algebra -- from Wolfram Library Archive |url=https://library.wolfram.com/infocenter/MathSource/4898/ |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=library.wolfram.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=quantum algebra in nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/quantum+algebra |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>

Subjects include:
*[[Quantum group]]s
*[[Skein theories]]
*[[Operadic algebra]]
*[[Diagrammatic algebra]]
*[[Quantum field theory]]
*[[Racks and quandles]]
